body:
> "specification-level" and "realm-agnostic" in the above-quoted text are undefined AFAICT in grovelling through HTML, Infra, WebIDL.

Well, at some point you kind of have to be able to draw conclusions based on the meanings of words :-/. 

"specification-level" is the same as "ground-level" or "high-level"; it's somethat that has meaning in a specific domain. In this case, the domain of specifications.

"realm agnostic" links to the definition of realm. "agnostic" means what it usually means: not tied to a specific one.

> also, perhaps "data structures and values" should be "types and data structures" ?

I don't think so. You can't manipulate a type in a spec, although you can manipulate a value.

> "specification-level" is the same as "ground-level" or "high-level"; it's somethat that has meaning in a specific domain. In this case, the domain of specifications.

of course. Though it would be helpful to explicitly characterize what comprises specification-level things. Perhaps they are the things one materializes in the context of one's spec that are not already defined in the whatwg specs other than [Infra](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/), and which may be defined in terms of types and data structures from Infra?

>  don't think so. You can't manipulate a type in a spec, although you can manipulate a value.

the full sentence that i am referring to is:
> You can, however, manipulate specification-level data structures and values from the [WHATWG Infra Standard](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/), as those are realm-agnostic.

The phrase "data structures and values from the WHATWG Infra Standard" seems odd because the latter does not define "values" per se. It defines primitive data types, and structures.

> Though it would be helpful to explicitly characterize what comprises specification-level things.

I don't think we can do that exhaustively. It's an intentionally vague term meant to allow freedom from specification writers.

> The phrase "data structures and values from the WHATWG Infra Standard" seems odd because the latter does not define "values" per se. It defines primitive data types, and structures.

In general, wherever there are types, there are values of their types. Again, we have to be able to assume people can infer these sorts of things.

---

I'll close this issue because I don't think there's anything unclear or ambiguous about the current text. Nevertheless, I appreciate your careful review, and will be visiting your other issues about it as well.
